creator: Jim’s Wormhole
description: Why are there jellyfish in the sky at the birth and the death of Jesus? A painting of the Virgin Mary, more than 500 years old, has a dark disc pouring out light, a man shielding his eyes, his dog staring up, and a cluster of tiny golden jellyfish in its sky. Nobody can even agree on who painted it. In Georgia, a cathedral said to hold the robe of Jesus has two jellyfish with faces at the crucifixion, painted on the tower where, legend says, a pillar of light once hung in the air. A monastery in Kosovo has the same scene from almost 700 years ago. A mysterious German book of omens from the 1500s painted one for the year 1007: a wondrous comet that "fell onto the earth". And the Bayeux Tapestry shows men pointing at one in the spring of 1066, months before England fell. It's on show in London right now. For a thousand years, people kept painting the same thing over their heads. What do you think they were really seeing? Follow @jimswormhole for more trips down the wormhole #jellyfish #ufo #uap #ancientmysteries #unexplained
headline: The Strange History Behind the “Jellyfish in the Sky” Theory
excerpt: A viral post links centuries-old imagery to a modern internet mystery.

creator: Hazalea𑣲𝒿
description: Chicken Aflredo Burritos✨🍗🌯#cookingtips #recipeideas #easyrecipes #DinnerIdeas  #foodasmr  Recipe:  For the chicken: * 2–3 chicken breasts, cut into bite-sized cubes * Olive oil * Onion powder * Garlic powder * Paprika * Italian seasoning * Salt and pepper For the creamy garlic Parmesan sauce: * 2 tbsp butter * ½ white or yellow onion, diced * 5 cloves garlic, minced * 1 tbsp flour * 1½–2 cups heavy cream * ½ cup grated Parmesan * 1 handful shredded cheese of choice * Italian seasoning * Salt and pepper For assembling: * medium flour tortillas * Shredded mozzarella * ¼ cup fresh parsley, chopped * Extra Parmesan for garnish Instructions 1. Cut 2–3 chicken breasts into bite-sized cubes. Drizzle with olive oil and season with onion powder, garlic powder, paprika, Italian seasoning, salt, and pepper. Mix until well coated. 2. Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chicken and cook until golden brown and the internal temperature reaches 165°F. Remove from the pan and set aside in a bowl. 3. In the same pan, melt 2 tbsp butter. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent. 4. Add the minced garlic and cook for about 30 seconds. Sprinkle in 1 tbsp flour and stir until everything is combined and the flour is cooked in. 5. Slowly pour in 1½–2 cups heavy cream. Add the Parmesan, shredded cheese, Italian seasoning, salt, and pepper. Stir everything together and let simmer until the sauce thickens slightly. 6. Pour about ¾ of the creamy sauce over the cooked chicken. Add ¼ cup chopped fresh parsley and mix until everything is evenly coated. 7. Add the chicken mixture to your tortillas, top with shredded mozzarella, and roll them up tightly. 8. Heat a little oil or butter in a skillet and fry the wraps on both sides until golden brown and crispy and the mozzarella is melted. 9. Garnish with fresh parsley and Parmesan. Serve with a side salad or broccoli and use the remaining creamy garlic Parmesan sauce for dipping!
